headline: Energy Stands Alone as Sellers Hold the Upper Hand
body_html:
Stocks are leaning lower at midday Friday, with decliners well ahead of advancers: 338 of the 544 names we track are down, against 201 higher. Prices are not final, but the tone is defensive, and energy is the only sector showing real momentum.

Energy is up 2.68%, led by oil-services names. Weatherford International has gained 7.34%, Schlumberger 6.65%, Valaris 6.64% and Innovex International 6.19%. Semiconductors are barely positive at 0.33%. Consumer is the weak spot, off 1.62%, with auto-parts makers Visteon, down 8.1%, and Gentex, down 7.2%, sliding. Bloom Energy is down 11.33%, the steepest drop on the board.

The standout mover is staffing firm Robert Half, up 21.76%. Into the close, watch whether the energy rally holds, whether the consumer slide widens with household sentiment near a record low ahead of the midterms, and whether Treasury yields hovering around 5% keep investors on the defensive. Monday, October 26, is the next trading day.

briefs.headline: Oil Services Lead the Tape
briefs.body: Oilfield contractors are doing the heavy lifting. Weatherford International is up 7.34%, Schlumberger 6.65%, Valaris 6.64% and Innovex International 6.19%. Together they push the energy group up 2.68%, easily the best sector so far. Whether the gains hold into the afternoon is the key question.

briefs.headline: Auto Suppliers Under Pressure
briefs.body: Auto-parts names are weighing on consumer stocks, which are down 1.62% as a group. Visteon is off 8.1% and Gentex 7.2%. Gentherm is a notable exception, up 7.23%, so the damage is uneven within the supplier chain.

briefs.headline: Robert Half Surges Past 21%
briefs.body: Staffing company Robert Half is the session's biggest gainer, up 21.76% in a market where most stocks are falling. A move that large on a weak tape sets it apart from every other name in our universe. Traders will watch whether it holds near the highs into the close.

briefs.headline: Yields Near 5% as Investors Seek Cover
briefs.body: The 10-year Treasury yield slipped back to 5% this week as investors looked for shelter from worries about artificial intelligence. That defensive stance fits a tape where sellers outnumber buyers. Credo Technology, down 6.81%, and Comfort Systems USA, down 6.39%, are among the weaker names.

briefs.headline: Sentiment Sours as Midterms Near
briefs.body: US consumer sentiment is hovering close to a record low ahead of the midterm elections, according to Reuters. Airlines face a related squeeze, with fewer people flying as fares climb, though carriers say they are unconcerned. Consumer stocks are the weakest group today.

briefs.headline: American Express Trims Staff, Banks Debate AI Risk
briefs.body: American Express plans to cut 5% of its workforce. Separately, analysts are debating whether Wall Street is overreacting to the idea that AI agents could pull deposits away from banks. Both stories point to a financial sector adjusting to new technology.
